instruction: I am organizing a get-together for my coworkers this Sunday night. I need to buy a return gift for everyone who has RSVPed yes on email. Buy a gift-wrapped 'Amazfit Band 5 Fitness Tracker' for each of them on amazon, and have them delivered to my home.
notes: Three apps: supervisor, gmail, amazon. The unknown number of coworkers who RSVPed yes is modeled as a discrete quantity object (qty-rsvp-yes) whose value is read at runtime by searching inbox threads for the get-together invitation and reading the thread's replies (a single representative thread object stands for all RSVP emails; at runtime the agent reads every relevant thread). That quantity is then used both for add_product_to_cart and add_gift_wrapping_to_product so ordered_quantity == gift_wrap_quantity == number of yes RSVPs. add_product_to_cart passes clear_cart_first=true so that pre-existing cart entries are not ordered. place_order requires the amazon address whose text matches the supervisor's home address (both supervisor.show_addresses and amazon.show_addresses are required) and a known payment card; no address is created/updated/deleted. The gmail/file_system record changes in the evaluation are side effects of placing the order (receipt email + attachment), not explicit steps. supervisor-complete-task takes the order record (product, quantity, address) as non-API parameters so its precondition equals the task-specific goal; it is called without an answer.
